cards.front: What three things identify a CloudWatch metric, and how many dimensions can it have?
cards.back: A **namespace** (for example `AWS/EC2`), a **metric name** (`CPUUtilization`) and zero or more **dimensions** (name/value pairs such as `InstanceId`). A metric can have **up to 30 dimensions**; each distinct combination is a separate metric.

cards.front: How often does EC2 send metrics with basic monitoring versus detailed monitoring?
cards.back: **Basic monitoring**: every **5 minutes**, free. **Detailed monitoring**: every **1 minute**, charged like metrics. Neither adds memory or disk-space metrics.

cards.front: You need EC2 memory (RAM) and file-system usage in CloudWatch. What do you do?
cards.back: Install the **unified CloudWatch agent** on the instance with an IAM role that has `CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy`. It publishes metrics such as `mem_used_percent` and `disk_used_percent` as **custom metrics** in the `CWAgent` namespace.

cards.front: Standard versus high-resolution custom metrics: what is the granularity of each?
cards.back: **Standard resolution**: 1-minute data. **High resolution**: **1-second** data (readable at 1, 5, 10, 30 s or multiples of 60). Data under 60 s is kept only 3 hours before being rolled up.

cards.front: How long does CloudWatch keep metric data?
cards.back: Up to **15 months**, rolled up over time: sub-minute data 3 hours, 1-minute data 15 days, 5-minute data 63 days, 1-hour data 455 days.

cards.front: What is a CloudWatch metric stream used for, and where can it send data?
cards.back: To push metric updates continuously (within minutes) instead of polling. Destinations: an **Amazon Data Firehose** stream (then S3, Redshift, OpenSearch, HTTP), a quick **S3** setup, or partners such as **Datadog, Dynatrace, Elastic, New Relic, Splunk, Sumo Logic**. Filters can include or exclude namespaces.
cards.updated: Kinesis Data Firehose is now Amazon Data Firehose; quick S3 and partner setups were added.

cards.front: Log group versus log stream in CloudWatch Logs?
cards.back: A **log stream** is the sequence of events from one source (an instance, container or file). A **log group** collects streams that share **retention, permissions, encryption and filters**, usually one per application.

cards.front: What is the default retention of a new log group, and what range can you set?
cards.back: Default: **never expire**. You can set **1 day up to 10 years** (3,653 days) per log group. Setting retention is the first fix for growing log storage costs.

cards.front: How is CloudWatch Logs data encrypted at rest?
cards.back: **Always encrypted** by default. For your own key, associate a **customer managed KMS key** with the log group (at creation or later via CLI/API); the key policy must allow the CloudWatch Logs service principal.

cards.front: Exporting CloudWatch Logs to S3: which API, and what is the delay?
cards.back: `CreateExportTask`, a **batch** export. Recently written events may wait as long as **12 hours** before an export task can include them, so it is never real time; use subscription filters for continuous delivery.

cards.front: Which destinations can a CloudWatch Logs subscription filter deliver to?
cards.back: **Kinesis Data Streams**, **Amazon Data Firehose**, **AWS Lambda** and **Amazon OpenSearch Service**. Events arrive base64-encoded and gzip-compressed, at least once.

cards.front: How many subscription filters can one log group have?
cards.back: **Up to five** per log group, plus one **account-level** subscription filter per Region that covers all log groups.
cards.updated: Older material says two per log group.

cards.front: Classic architecture to centralize logs from many accounts and Regions into S3?
cards.back: Subscription filter in each sender account → a CloudWatch Logs **destination** (one per Region) in the central account with an access policy → **Kinesis Data Streams** → **Data Firehose** → **S3**.

cards.front: What is CloudWatch Logs Insights, and what is it not?
cards.back: An interactive **query engine** over stored logs with automatic field discovery, filters, stats, saved queries and dashboard widgets, even across accounts. It is **not a real-time** alerting engine; it is billed per GB scanned.

cards.front: How do you raise an alarm when the word ERROR appears in application logs?
cards.back: Create a **metric filter** on the log group (pattern such as `ERROR` or `{ $.level = "ERROR" }`), which publishes a custom metric, then a **CloudWatch alarm** on that metric with an SNS action. Filters only count new events.

cards.front: Old CloudWatch Logs agent versus unified CloudWatch agent?
cards.back: The **old Logs agent** sent only logs and is now **deprecated and unsupported**. The **unified agent** sends logs **and** in-guest metrics (RAM, disk, processes, swap, netstat), supports StatsD/collectd, and can load its config from **SSM Parameter Store**.
cards.updated: The old logs-only agent is now documented as deprecated and no longer supported.

cards.front: What are the three CloudWatch alarm states?
cards.back: **OK** (within threshold), **ALARM** (breaching), **INSUFFICIENT_DATA** (just created, metric missing, or not enough data).

cards.front: List the action types a CloudWatch metric alarm can take.
cards.back: Notify an **SNS** topic, invoke a **Lambda** function, **EC2** stop/terminate/reboot/recover, an **Auto Scaling** policy, create a Systems Manager **OpsItem** or **incident**, start an investigation. State changes also go to EventBridge.
cards.updated: Direct Lambda, Systems Manager and investigation actions were added after the original EC2/ASG/SNS list.

cards.front: What period can an alarm on a 1-second (high-resolution) metric use?
cards.back: **10, 20 or 30 seconds** (a high-resolution alarm, charged more) or any multiple of 60 seconds.
cards.updated: The 20-second option is newer than the slides, which list 10 or 30 seconds.

cards.front: What is a composite alarm and why use one?
cards.back: An alarm whose rule combines the **states of other alarms** with **AND, OR, NOT**. It reduces **alarm noise** by notifying only when a meaningful combination occurs. It can notify SNS, invoke Lambda or create OpsItems, but **cannot do EC2 or Auto Scaling actions**.

cards.front: Which metric and action make an EC2 instance recover onto new hardware, and what does it keep?
cards.back: An alarm on **StatusCheckFailed_System** with the **recover** action. The instance keeps its **instance ID, private/public/Elastic IPs, metadata, placement group, EBS volumes and AZ**; RAM (and instance store) data is lost.

cards.front: How do you test an alarm's notification path without a real incident?
cards.back: `aws cloudwatch set-alarm-state --alarm-name <name> --state-value ALARM --state-reason "test"`. The alarm runs its actions, then returns to its real state at the next evaluation.

cards.front: What does CloudWatch Network Synthetic Monitor measure, and does it need agents?
cards.back: **Round-trip latency and packet loss** (plus a network health indicator) from a VPC subnet to on-premises IPs over **Direct Connect or Site-to-Site VPN**, using ICMP or TCP probes. **No agents**; results are CloudWatch metrics.

cards.front: What are the two kinds of EventBridge rule, and how many targets can a rule have?
cards.back: A rule with an **event pattern** (react when matching events arrive) or a **schedule** (cron or rate). Each rule can send to **up to 5 targets**. For new schedules AWS recommends **EventBridge Scheduler**.
cards.updated: Scheduled rules are now labelled legacy in favour of EventBridge Scheduler.

cards.front: Default, partner and custom event buses: what does each receive?
cards.back: **Default**: events from AWS services in your account. **Partner**: events from SaaS partners. **Custom**: events your own applications publish with `PutEvents`.

cards.front: What do EventBridge archive and replay give you?
cards.back: An **archive** stores all or pattern-filtered events from a bus for N days or indefinitely. A **replay** re-sends a time window of archived events to the **same source bus** (marked with `replay-name`), for example after fixing a consumer bug.

cards.front: What is the EventBridge schema registry for?
cards.back: It holds schemas for AWS events, can **infer schemas** from events on a bus (schema discovery) with **versioning**, and generates **code bindings** so applications know the event structure in advance.

cards.front: How do you collect events from every account of an organization into one event bus?
cards.back: Put a **resource-based policy** on a central bus allowing `events:PutEvents` from the accounts or organization (`aws:PrincipalOrgID`), and in each account create a rule whose target is that bus (with an IAM role).

cards.front: Container Insights versus Lambda Insights?
cards.back: **Container Insights**: metrics and logs for **ECS, EKS, Kubernetes on EC2 and Fargate** (containerized agent on Kubernetes). **Lambda Insights**: per-function CPU time, memory, disk, network and **cold starts**, delivered as a **Lambda layer**.

cards.front: Contributor Insights versus Application Insights?
cards.back: **Contributor Insights** finds **top-N contributors** in log data (top IPs, hosts, error URLs). **Application Insights** builds **automated problem dashboards** for EC2-based apps (.NET, IIS, SQL Server, Java…) and related AWS resources, sending findings to EventBridge and OpsCenter.
